title: onprem-airgap-offline-bundle-vendor-rke2-suse-microos-tuf-updates
author: Olivia Chen
release_notes: Update offline bundle vendoring and TUF metadata for rke2 + SUSE MicroOS; fixes post-install checksum failures in air-gapped installs. No breaking changes.
body: Background: Customers running the on-prem air-gapped installer on SUSE MicroOS+rke2 were seeing intermittent TUF metadata validation failures during bundle extraction after recent upstream packaging changes. This caused a class of post-install verification failures and made upgrades fragile in offline environments. Motivation: Patch the vendored packages and TUF metadata generation so offline bundles remain reproducible and validate correctly across supported kube distros (rke2, k3s) and SUSE MicroOS variants. Summary of changes: - Regenerated offline bundle including updated rke2 binaries (v1.25.11+rke2r1) and matching container images packaged into the bundle. - Reworked vendoring script to pin Debian/Ubuntu/RHEL/SUSE mirrors and include checksums for each archive artifact. - TUF metadata pipeline: fixed timestamp/targets expiry handling and aligned snapshot generation with tuf v0.20 semantics used by our offline installer. - Added distro-specific packaging hooks for SUSE MicroOS (initrd tweaks, kernel module ordering) and a validation step in the installer to skip unsupported kernel module loading on older MicroOS kernels. - Added CI job (airgap-bundle-validate) that runs bundle validation with TUF verification and a smoke install in a local rke2 single-node VM. - Docs: updated onprem/airgap/README with upgrade instructions and rollback tooling notes. Checklist: - [x] Reproduce failure locally with previous bundle - [x] Regenerate vendor artifacts with pinned mirrors - [x] Add snapshot/timestamp fixes for TUF - [x] Add CI validation job - [x] Run installer smoke test (rke2 single-node VM) - [x] Obtain reviews and sign-off from infra/security Testing notes: I iterated on the TUF metadata locally by running tuf-util generate-snapshot and generate-timestamp against a mirror of the bundle contents and confirmed that the installer validates the snapshot and targets manifest on first-run install and on subsequent upgrades. The CI job simulates an air-gapped verification by using the restarted TUF server and verifying expiration handling across time-skewed clocks (30s drift). Rollforward/rollback: The installer was updated to keep the previous bundle archive in /var/lib/redwood/offline-bundles/previous.tar.gz and to perform a checksum comparison before attempting an upgrade. If TUF verification fails during upgrade, the installer aborts and restores the previous bundle state, then emits a clear diagnostics blob to /var/log/redwood/installer/rollback.log. Upgrade notes for operators: - For SUSE MicroOS customers: run the installer with --kernel-mod-order=compat if you are on kernels older than 5.15. This is a safe default for affected kernels and will be selected automatically when the installer detects the kernel range. - If you previously hit TUF metadata expiration errors, download the regenerated bundle (sha256: abcdef1234567890...) and re-run installer with --reverify-bundle. Backwards compatibility: The changes are additive — existing bundles and non-SUSE installs are unaffected. The vendoring script defaults are unchanged for Ubuntu/RHEL but include the new pinned mirrors for reproducibility. Related: ENG-5412 (airgap install failures), SUP-2234 (customer support ticket reproducing issue).
